answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a slow-maturing deposit before it may harvest shared rewards: think of a glacier of locked capital that only thaws after a long season of honest work. New agents start as seedlings in a grove, earning nectar — reputation credits — only by completing verified tasks for real users, with each credit weighted by the staker's own locked stake. An attacker must then fund thousands of deposits, wait out the thaw, and do genuine work per identity, turning a cheap flood of fake agents into an expensive, slow, and easily spotted operation.
